text:
maya: Acme Ops reported a sudden spike of 5xx/timeouts on hosted inference starting ~10:23 UTC. They see a lot of SDK retries and p95 latency jumps. Customer says ~20% of requests get 502/504.

sam_acme: posting sample logs they captured: `2026-03-14T10:24:05Z ERROR request failed status=502 id=abc123` and a short curl repro they ran locally.

sam_acme: curl -i --http2 -H 'Authorization: Bearer <token>' "https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate" -d '{"input":"hello"}'

leo: thanks — looks bad. first quick questions: did you see any deploys or infra changes around 10:15-10:25? can you share the full SDK log snippet (including retry headers)?

maya: @taylor were there any deploys?

deploy-bot: deploy finished: service=hosted-gateway sha=abcde123 time=2026-03-14T10:14:52Z (canary -> stable) :rocket:

leo: OK noted. I'll pull edge proxy traces for that window. initial hypothesis: client retry fanout + long-lived http2 streams + connection churn at the proxy causing connection pool exhaustion -> 5xxs. Also want to check auth token refresh timing (we saw this pattern before).

taylor: pulling traces now, also seeing a burst of auth refresh calls for that tenant between 10:22-10:26. sending logs to thread.

leo: Sam, could you run this quick repro (low-effort): a small loop that does 50 concurrent requests with default SDK retry logic for 2 minutes, and attach your SDK debug trace? this will help us reproduce the client-side fanout. Example node snippet: ```
const http2 = require('http2');
// simplified pseudo-repro — use official SDK with debug=1 for real logs
async function load() {
  // spawn 50 concurrent promises calling /v1/generate
}
load();
```

sam_acme: running now. also attaching tcpdump output and edge_trace IDs.

leo: quick find from edge logs: during the spike the gateway outbound pool hit max connections to the inference backends for that AZ, and we started returning 502s. The auth service also showed a brief ~10s saturation (504s) coincident with a token refresh fanout for that tenant. Suspect: token refresh + default aggressive SDK retries without jitter = synchronized retry storms.

maya: what can we tell the customer now? they asked if this is on our side and if it's recurring.

leo: actionable short-term mitigation for Acme: 1) set client concurrency to <=10, 2) add jittered exponential backoff on retries, 3) temporarily disable aggressive connection multiplexing in their SDK (or upgrade to latest SDK which includes backoff fixes). We can also apply a short-term server-side tenant-level soft-rate-limit to smooth requests while we remediate.

maya: drafted customer note: "We're seeing a request retry storm from your SDK causing proxy pool contention which resulted in elevated 5xxs. Immediate mitigations: reduce concurrency and enable jittered backoff. We're applying a smoothing rate-limit now and will follow up with a permanent fix." want me to send? :email:

sam_acme: send please. we'll also roll an internal fix that adds jitter on refresh. thanks.

leo: platform mitigation steps I'm doing now: 1) bump gateway outbound connection pool for impacted AZ (temporary), 2) apply per-tenant smoothing rate limiter at ingress (10s window), 3) pin failing requests to a fallback model variant to reduce backend load. will monitor p95/p99.

leo: repro notes we logged: - reproduce with http2 multiplexed client doing high concurrent short requests (observed in customer's node/python SDK) - remove client-side sync retry behavior and add jitter to avoid synchronized replays - token refresh flows should be staggered (randomized ttl refresh)

maya: customer update sent at 10:58 UTC saying we're applying temporary smoothing and asking them to throttle client concurrency.

sam_acme: received update, currently throttling to 8 concurrent and seeing error rate drop to ~2%. thanks for the fast turnaround.

taylor: follow-ups: (a) schedule a postmortem w/ infra + sdk team to harden backoff defaults, (b) add tenant-level auto-smoothing if we see repeated token-fanout patterns, owner=leo, eta=48h, (c) educate SDK docs about recommended concurrency/backoff.

leo: I'll take (a) and (b). maya please own customer comms and close once ACME confirms stability.

maya: noted, will close after 24h stable window. :thumbsup:

sre-bot: alert cleared for tenant=acme-corp window=2026-03-14T10:20:00Z-2026-03-14T11:00:00Z

maya: closing thread once we confirm 24h stable. thanks all.
